headline: Adopted Space Savers ordinance, reconsidered $249,708 HHS lease funding, authorized Degmar lease and Rourke Bridge agreement, and approved several grants.
summary: Members adopted an ordinance amending Chapter 266-61 on space savers, held hearings on several utility petitions that were referred to the Wire Inspector, and reconsidered a $249,708 transfer for the HHS lease. They also accepted grants for 911 services, MCOA, and technology, authorized a lease with Degmar Development Corporation, authorized an agreement with MassDOT for the Rourke Bridge, and referred numerous resident requests on traffic, housing, and historic preservation to the City Manager.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the Non-Profit Organization SC July 28th meeting and the City Council Regular Meeting of July 28th, 10-0 roll call vote.
Adopted the ordinance amending Chapter 266-61 on space savers, 10-0 roll call vote.
Referred utility petitions from Boston Gas and National Grid (Items #5.1 to #5.6) to the Wire Inspector for report and recommendation.
Reconsidered and re-adopted the $249,708 Supplemental Appropriation transfer for the HHS Lease, 10-0 roll call vote.
Referred request for a Transportation Engineer update on safety improvements at Princeton Boulevard and Foster Street to the City Manager.
Referred request for Rules SC review of City Council rules and subcommittee structure to the City Manager.
Referred request for a report on enforcement of the city's vacancy ordinance at 50 Warren St. to the City Manager.
Referred request to explore traffic calming measures at Chapel and Elm Streets to the City Manager.
Referred request for a report on criminal background check practices for positions involving children or vulnerable populations to the City Manager.
Referred proposal for a pilot program redesigning subcommittees and scheduling to the City Manager, then referred the matter to the Rules SC.
Referred request to install a flashing all-way stop at the bottom of Mt. Pleasant and 1st Street Blvd. to the City Manager.
Referred request to install a flashing LED speed sign on Varnum Ave. to the City Manager.
Referred request for a detailed report on the city's sewage capacity to the City Manager.
Referred request for a report on pros and cons of an ordinance closing all bars and restaurants at midnight to the City Manager, adopted 10-0 roll call vote.
Referred request to work with the National Park Service to recognize the Ladd and Whitney Monument as a National Historic Landmark to the City Manager.
Referred request to work with the Lowell Historic Board to restore and enlarge the portrait of Mayor Charles D. Palmer to the City Manager.
Adopted vote to accept gift of Commemorative Bicentennial Plaque, 10-0 roll call vote.
Adopted vote to accept/expend $1,048.95 State 911 Department Emergency Medical Dispatch Grant, 10-0 roll call vote.
Adopted vote to accept/expend $25k MCOA Grant, 10-0 roll call vote.
Adopted vote to accept/expend $40k EOTSS Grant – MIS, 10-0 roll call vote.
Adopted vote to accept/expend $51,424.73 State 911 Department Training Grant, 10-0 roll call vote.
Adopted vote to accept/expend $540,496 State 911 Department Support and Incentive Grant, 10-0 roll call vote.
Adopted vote authorizing the City Manager to execute a Lease Agreement with Degmar Development Corporation, 10-0 roll call vote.
Adopted vote authorizing the City Manager to execute an NPA with MassDOT for the Rourke Bridge, 10-0 roll call vote.
Adopted the Order for a 60 Day Trial, 10-0 roll call vote.
Accepted and adopted Wire Inspector Reports on National Grid utility pole installations at Westford Street/15 Technology Drive and at 1270 and 1299 Westford Street.
Referred three property damage claims to the Law Department for report and recommendation.
Referred Vidong Pich's (FORKIN Mill City) request for an overhanging sign at 108 Merrimack Street to the Law Department.
Referred Kelly Valencia's request for traffic safety improvements on Whipple Street to the Transportation Engineer.
Referred Maureen Joubert's request for a speed bump on Laurie Lane to the Transportation Engineer.
Referred National Grid's request for a new utility pole at 480 Westford Street to a Public Hearing on August 25, 2026.

Motion by C. Robinson, seconded by C. Nuon to suspend rules to allow 
speaker, Tareena Pagan, to address Council regarding recent Puerto 
Rican Festival in Lowell.  So voted.  Ms. Pagan commented about the 
disappointment with coordination with the City regarding the length of the 
event and that there needs to be more transparency with the process.  Ms. 
Pagan commented on the importance of the festival and that the goal is to 
have open communication with the City moving forward so that process will
be better in the future.  Ms. Pagan noted that community is always 
available to participate in the process.  C. Robinson noted he was not sure 
of issues and that miscommunication caused financial issues for the event 
and that the City was the one who set the dates for the festival.  C. 
Robinsopn noted a better set-up was needed.  Melissa Desroches 
(Communications Team) noted the issue and the permitting process and 
that permits were not fully procured for the two days.  C. McDonough 
commented that it should be clear to all event organizers that if money is 
not paid for permits there will be no event.  C. Chau noted the need for 
clean path forward.  C. Liang noted cultural events are important and that 
the needs to be best efforts by the City.  Motion by C. Robinson, seconded
by C. Chau to allow speaker, Elizabeth Gonzalez, to address the Council.  
Ms. Gonzalez noted she was president of the organization and commented
on the process noting there was a lot of misinformation about the event and
that the event was a success.  Ms. Gonzalez noted that the loss of day of 
the event causes some financial constraints but that all money will be 
refunded if owed.  Ms. Gonzalez noted payment to City for permits and 
police details and that a lot of time and effort was put forth by the 
committee to ensure a great event.

6.11. M. Gitschier - Req. City Mgr. provide the City Council with a 
report on the pros and cons of creating an ordinance closing all bars 
and restaurants at midnight throughout the City.
In City Council, seconded by C. Nuon, referred to City Manager. Adopted 
per Roll Call vote 10 yeas (C. Chau, C. Descoteaux, M. Gitschier, C. Juran,
C. Liang, C. McDonough, C. Mercier, C. Nuon, C. Robinson, C. Rourke), 1 
absent (C. Scott).  So voted.  C. Descoteaux noted the negative responses 
regarding the motion and requested some clarity.  Chair relinquished to 
Vice Chair Nuon at 8:10 PM.  M. Gitschier commented most places are 
closed by then and that the police are understaffed to monitor on the late 
shift.  M. Gitschier noted the environment changes in that area after 
midnight.  M. Gitschier noted motion was just to weigh the pros and cons 
and make a decision.   C. Descoteaux noted it could stifle investment 
downtown.  C. Robinson noted he was fine with a report and that action 
depends on the environment and that good business should not be 
penalized due to bad business.  C. McDonough noted the need for 
information to assess needs.  C. Mercier noted prior request regarding
information on bars and restaurants.  C. Chau questioned the impact on 
small business.

Building.

voted.  C. McDonough noted the number of historic monuments in the City
and that there should be a dedicated staff member for their oversight.
